editorial.headline: Used Motorcycle Wholesale: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Used-motorcycle wholesale is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s risk-class moratorium blocks PMA registration for it.
editorial.body:
Wholesale trade in used motorcycles, including motorised bicycles and mopeds, is the commercial terrain of this activity. Its language is deliberately wholesale: it is concerned with the trade in previously owned two-wheelers at that level of commerce. That category extends beyond motorcycles alone, since motorised bicycles and mopeds are expressly included. The record places the activity within a practical set of business sizes—Micro, Small, Medium and Large—so its definition is not confined to one scale. For a founder, that gives the activity a clear frame before the investment question begins: used two-wheelers, traded wholesale, across the named scale categories.

Nationally, that investment question has an unambiguous answer. The PMA status is open, and foreign ownership may reach 100%. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The 100% figure is the stated foreign-ownership ceiling; it is not a number that needs to be inferred. National openness, however, should not be mistaken for a blanket geographical assurance. The Bali entry carries a separate result, drawn from the activity’s OSS risk classification and the province’s rule.

Bali is where the answer changes sharply. The Bali status is blocked by risk class. At the Large scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope in the record. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. On the facts supplied here, that prohibition applies to this activity. A foreign investor therefore cannot register it in Bali through a PMA business today, even though the national PMA position is open and permits up to 100% foreign ownership.

The useful reading is not to dilute either side of the record. There is a national pathway characterised by an open PMA status and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In Bali, there is a different present result: blocked PMA registration, because the activity falls within the risk bands captured by the provincial moratorium. This distinction is the centre of the entry, not a footnote to it. Anyone evaluating wholesale trade in used motorcycles, motorised bicycles and mopeds should hold both statements together: the national investment setting is open; Bali does not allow a PMA registration for the activity.
